newsitem.title: USA: Pacific Rehab sees Q4 EPS $0.04 - $0.05.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Rehab sees Q4 EPS $0.04 - $0.05.

text.p: Pacific Rehabilitation & Sports Medicine Inc said it expects a fourth quarter profit of $0.04 to $0.05 a share due to the effect of accounting charges taken in the third quarter ended September 30.
It said a charge for accounts receivable taken in the third quarter will have a "going forward" effect of about $100,000 in future quarters on net revenue and pre-tax income.

Late Thursday, the provider of physical therapy services, reported a third quarter loss of $0.58 a share versus a $0.02 share profit last year. Third quarter 1996 included charges over $5.0 million, or about $0.61 a share, after taxes.
The company said it does not expect any additional charges in the current fourth quarter, and it does not anticipate closing or consolidating any more of its therapeutic clinics.
Pacific Rehablilitation said it believes it has closed all unprofitable clinics in the company. It currently operates 66 outpatient clinics in several western and southern states.

"It will take us until the first quarter of 1997 to completely return California (operations) to profitability, and by then, we expect each of our clinics to be profitable," Chief Executive Bill Barancik said in a statement.
Third quarter charges included contract and bad debt allowance provisions, restructuring costs, a provision for losses on the sale of clinics in Texas and the settlement of certain claims.
